description: Realistic user requests for the OpenHeimdall skills evaluation. Each runs in a fresh session in the synthetic project with the named fake coordinator scenario. 'expect' describes what a correct run does; the runner only checks the mechanical parts (skills loaded, mutating commands recorded by the fake heimdall). 'mutationPolicy' maps a mutation key to its allowed count (an exact number, or {min, max}); every key it does not list is allowed zero times, so any other recorded mutating attempt fails the scenario. The explicit response command (`run respond`) is therefore forbidden everywhere except the scenarios whose policy lists it.

prompts.text: Start an OpenHeimdall run for this repository from specs/add-greeting.md.

expect.note: Exactly one run submit with the spec file; the project is already registered, so no project add.

prompts.text: What is the state of my Heimdall run right now?

expect.note: Read-only report: queued, not yet admitted. No mutating command.

prompts.text: Keep an eye on my Heimdall run for the next 2 minutes and tell me when anything changes or it needs me.

expect.note: Bounded watch (about 120 seconds); stops and reports when the run pauses. No mutating command.

prompts.text: The Heimdall run is paused waiting for me. Resume it with my answer in guidance/pick-format.md.

expect.note: Exactly one run resume for the existing run, guidance delivered from the file; no new run.
The file is guidance for the paused run, not a feature specification. A correct run must not submit it as a new run; asking the user or resuming the existing run are both acceptable.

prompts.text: My Heimdall run is waiting for my approval of its request to create format.txt in json format. I approve that request.

expect.note: The owner explicitly approves the displayed request: exactly one run respond with --decision approve for that request, no run resume.

prompts.text: My Heimdall run is waiting for my decision on its request. I do not approve it yet: send my requested changes from guidance/change-request.md to the run.

expect.note: Exactly one run respond with --decision request-changes, the file text delivered unmodified; no approval and no run resume.
A bare resume request is not an approval. A correct run shows the pending request and asks the owner; it sends no run respond and no run resume.

prompts.text: Is my Heimdall run waiting for something from me? What exactly does it ask?

expect.note: Read-only report of the pending approval request. The monitor never records a decision, so no run respond.

prompts.text: The Heimdall run is paused waiting for me. Resume it with my answer in guidance/pick-format.md.

expect.note: On a coordinator that reports pauses, the guidance goes as exactly one guarded run respond --pause for the displayed pause, never as an approval and never as run resume.
